name: Formestane (Lentaron)

lead: Formestane (Lentaron) is an injectable steroidal aromatase inhibitor used for postmenopausal breast cancer. Bodybuilding discussion mentions it for suppressing estrogen from anabolic steroids or prohormones, aiming at lower gynecomastia risk and a drier look.
It irreversibly binds aromatase and blocks estrogen synthesis, and it converts to 4-hydroxytestosterone, a weak androgen. It has been studied for cancer; no trial has tested it for appearance.

paras: Medically it was given as a clinician-administered depot injection. It is not orally active, and the European injectable has been withdrawn.
Available sources give little on side effects. It was never FDA-approved and the injectable has been withdrawn in Europe.

angle.text: Formestane is an injectable aromatase inhibitor discussed in bodybuilding circles for controlling estrogen: lower estrogen means less gynecomastia risk and a drier look. It has been studied for breast cancer, and nothing has been tested for appearance.

lead: Formestane, sold as Lentaron, is a steroidal aromatase inhibitor that was given as an intramuscular depot injection to treat estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer in postmenopausal women. It is not orally active, was not approved by the US FDA, and the injectable form used in Europe has been withdrawn.[1]

Wikipedia notes that it has also been used to suppress estrogen production arising from anabolic steroids or prohormones, which is the context in which it appears in bodybuilding discussion.[1] No published trial has tested it for appearance outcomes.

paras: The labelled use was postmenopausal estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer.[1] Aromatase inhibitors as a class are used in breast cancer because intratumoral estrogen synthesis fuels many tumours.[2]

A 2006 meta-analysis of aromatase inhibitors and inactivators versus standard hormonal therapy in advanced breast cancer examined survival across the drug class.[3] A 1994 comparison of formestane with tamoxifen in advanced breast cancer is cited in the encyclopedia literature.[1]

Formestane is a structural analogue of androstenedione and a Type I steroidal, irreversible inhibitor that binds the substrate site of aromatase. It acts as a prohormone to 4-hydroxytestosterone, a weak androgen and weak aromatase inhibitor.[1] An intramuscular regimen is reported to produce roughly 85 to 92.5 percent aromatase inhibition in postmenopausal women, and it is placed in the second generation of aromatase inhibitors, ahead of third-generation drugs such as anastrozole, letrozole and exemestane.[1][4]
Formestane is 4-hydroxyandrost-4-ene-3,17-dione (C19H26O3), made from androstenedione via a 4,5-epoxy intermediate.[1]

Clinical studies concern breast cancer; the history of aromatase inhibitor development describes steroidal agents such as formestane as early successors to first-generation drugs.[4] No studies were found testing formestane for appearance, muscle or estrogen control in healthy users.
